method: Structured JSON from the Gemini API, instructed by docs/PROJECT_VISION.md@main blob fe2f414774b7. Independently reviewed by Claude on 2026-11-13: every record was re-checked against pages opened in that run, replacing an earlier keyword-only pass. characters.summary: Duke Nukem fights an alien invasion of Earth with conventional firearms and exotic weapons: the Devastator double rocket launcher, the RPG, the Freezethrower, the Shrink Ray and remote pipe bombs. Inventory items add a jetpack, a Holoduke decoy, speed-boosting steroids and body armor. He defeats the Battlelord, the Overlord, the Cycloid Emperor and the Alien Queen.

techniques: Shrink Ray (shrinks enemies to be stomped)

weaknesses: His own RPG can kill him if a rocket misfires or detonates close by
limitations: Holoduke decoy lasts only a limited time

sources.supports: Alien invasion plot; pistol, shotgun, Devastator, RPG, Freezethrower, Shrink Ray and pipe bombs; Holoduke, steroids (speed), jetpack (flight within levels) and body armor; episode bosses Battlelord, Overlord, Cycloid Emperor and Alien Queen

feats.claim: Defeated the Cycloid Emperor, the final and most powerful boss of the original three episodes
Defeated the Alien Queen in an underwater cave while she spawned Protector Drones

notableResults.note: Episode 1 boss with a chaingun-grenade launcher and very high health
Alien leader on the Moon, armed with a dual rocket launcher
Final boss of the original three episodes; fires fast missiles and plasma

campaignTags.claim: Uses the Holoduke decoy and the jetpack
The Freezethrower fires ice crystals that freeze victims solid

unknowns: Other games (Duke Nukem II, Forever, spin-offs) are not covered by this record.

Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): replaced the unopened Wikipedia cite with Giant Bomb's Duke Nukem 3D page. Corrected steroids from 'resilience' to a temporary speed boost (that is what the source says). Removed the unsourced 'arrogance' and 'environmental hazards' weaknesses and the jetpack-fuel limit, and dropped 'saved Earth multiple times'. Added the four episode bosses and the ice-weapon tag (Freezethrower).

characters.continuity: The Last of Us Part II
characters.summary: Ellie is a smaller, lighter fighter than Abby who relies on stealth, distance and explosives: she hides prone in tall grass, crafts Molotov cocktails, uses a bow and firearms, and carries her switchblade. She kills dozens of WLF soldiers on her revenge hunt and, in the final fight in Santa Barbara, overpowers Abby and starts drowning her before choosing to let her go.

mechanisms: Stealth: crouching or going prone in tall grass to hide
Small size lets her squeeze through tight gaps

weaknesses: Enemies can still spot her at close range even when she hides in grass
limitations: Unenhanced human physicality: smaller and lighter than Abby, so she leans on stealth, distance and explosives

sources.supports: Ellie relies on stealth, distance and explosives; hides prone in tall grass; crafts Molotovs; unbreakable switchblade; bow; can swim; the theater cat-and-mouse with Abby; the Santa Barbara fight in the surf where Ellie loses two fingers
Santa Barbara fight: Ellie gains the upper hand and starts drowning Abby, then spares her; WLF members could seek revenge for Ellie killing dozens of their soldiers

feats.claim: Killed dozens of WLF soldiers during her revenge hunt
feats.citation: The Last of Us Part II

notableResults.citation: The Last of Us Part II (Santa Barbara)
notableResults.note: Both badly hurt; Ellie lost two fingers to a bite but gained the upper hand and began drowning Abby, then chose to spare her and let her leave with Lev

campaignTags.claim: Hides prone in tall grass and stalks Abby in a stealth cat-and-mouse fight in the theater

unknowns: The earlier theater fight with Abby (played as Abby) is not recorded as a result: the opened pages describe it only as a cat-and-mouse fight and do not state its outcome.

Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): replaced the unopened Wikipedia cite with TV Tropes and GamesRadar pages that cover Ellie's play style and the ending. Changed the Abby result from 'inconclusive ... ceasefire of exhaustion' to a win: Ellie overpowered Abby and spared her. Removed the 'Seraphite/infected hordes' wording, 'dodge maneuvers' and the 'switchblade can break' limit (the source calls it unbreakable). Removed the immunity unknown: it is not a combat factor here.

characters.summary: Ezio is a Renaissance master assassin who fights with the hidden blade(s), the poison blade, a hidden gun, a crossbow, throwing knives and smoke bombs. He blends with crowds to escape guards and flew Leonardo's flying machine over Venice. In the Sistine Chapel he beat Rodrigo Borgia in a bare-handed brawl and spared him.
weaknesses: Not established by the opened sources (an unenhanced human without Piece of Eden protection)
limitations: Much of his toolkit (second hidden blade, poison blade, hidden gun) depends on devices Leonardo builds from Codex pages
Consumables (medicine, poison, throwing knives, smoke bombs, bullets) must be restocked

sources.supports: Rodrigo nearly defeated Ezio at their first encounter and fled when Ezio's allies arrived; in the Vatican Ezio emerged victorious over Rodrigo wielding the Staff of Eden and spared him; Apple of Eden

Leonardo built the hidden blade(s), poison blade and hidden gun; flying machine over Venice; blending with crowds and courtesans to evade guards; horse riding; Sistine Chapel fight: Apple creates four copies of Ezio, Rodrigo turns invisible with the Staff, Ezio lays down arms for a brawl and spares him
Ezio challenges Pope Rodrigo Borgia to a fistfight inside the Sistine Chapel ('No more weapons') and spares him
Brotherhood weapons: hidden blade, poison darts, crossbow for silent kills
AC II equipment: second hidden blade, poison blade, pistol; stocks of medicine, poison, throwing knives and smoke bombs

feats.claim: After a Piece-of-Eden duel in the Sistine Chapel, laid down his weapons and beat Rodrigo Borgia (Pope Alexander VI) in a bare-handed brawl
Escaped a guard patrol by blending in with a group of courtesans

notableResults.note: Rodrigo almost defeated Ezio and fled when Ezio's allies arrived
Rodrigo used the Staff of Eden (incl. invisibility) and took the Apple; Ezio then won a fist fight and spared him

conditional.dependsOn: Leonardo's flying machine lifted by bonfire heat

campaignTags.claim: Evaded Dante's patrol by blending in with Teodora's courtesans; crowd blending is part of his training
Uses Leonardo-built hidden blades, poison blade and hidden gun, plus smoke bombs

unknowns: Brotherhood/Revelations gear such as the parachute and hookblade is not covered by the opened pages and was left out.

Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): replaced the unopened Wikipedia cite with an opened Wikipedia mirror, the Assassin's Creed Wiki, FandomWire, StrategyWiki and Gamepressure. Corrected the Rodrigo fight: it happened in the Sistine Chapel (not 'outside the Vault'), after Rodrigo used the Staff of Eden, and Ezio spared him. Added the first encounter (inconclusive: Rodrigo nearly beat Ezio, then fled). Removed 'parachute gliding' and the unsourced firearms weakness. Tags stealth and gadgets kept.

characters.continuity: League of Legends (current lore, post-2018 update)
characters.summary: Ezreal is an explorer who found a bronze Shuriman gauntlet in the tomb of the tyrant Ne'Zuk. The gauntlet siphons and amplifies his own essence into arcane blasts. In play he fires Mystic Shot, Essence Flux and Trueshot Barrage and blinks short distances with Arcane Shift.

techniques: Arcane Shift (blink, then a homing bolt)
Trueshot Barrage (wide energy barrage that hits every unit it passes through)

mechanisms: Arcane Shift short-range teleport to escape

weaknesses: Not established by the opened sources
limitations: His arcane blasts are channeled through the gauntlet, which siphons and amplifies his own essence

sources.supports: Official bio: raids catacombs and uses his mystical Shuriman gauntlet to unleash arcane blasts; ability names Mystic Shot, Essence Flux, Arcane Shift, Trueshot Barrage
2018 bio: found the bronze gauntlet in Ne'Zuk's tomb; it siphons and amplifies his essence; he used it to blast through the tomb's traps
Ability descriptions: Mystic Shot energy bolt; E teleports him to a nearby location and fires a homing arrow; Trueshot Barrage energy missiles damage each unit they pass through

feats.claim: Found the gauntlet in the tomb of the Shuriman tyrant Ne'Zuk and used it at once to blast through the tomb's traps

campaignTags.claim: Unleashes arcane blasts through a mystical Shuriman gauntlet
Arcane Shift teleports him to a nearby location

unknowns: Whether Ezreal can teleport without the gauntlet is not stated by the opened sources.
Giant Bomb's lore section is the pre-2018 'amulet' biography; only its ability descriptions are used here.

Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): replaced the unopened fandom and generic League of Legends cites with the official champion page, the 2018 bio and Giant Bomb. Corrected the feat to the tomb of Ne'Zuk. Removed the invalid 'flight: Not applicable' tag and the game-balance weaknesses ('fragile', 'relies on aiming').

characters.continuity: Star Fox series (Star Fox 64, Star Fox: Assault)
characters.summary: Falco is Fox McCloud's wingman, a brash, cocky and highly skilled Arwing pilot. In Star Fox: Assault he stays in his Arwing as the team's air support while the Star Fox team fights the Aparoid invasion through to the Aparoid homeworld.

techniques: Barrel roll that deflects enemy fire

limitations: Fights from his Arwing; the opened sources describe no on-foot combat in the mainline games

sources.supports: Fox's wingman; brash and cocky; one of the most skilled pilots on the team; ace pilot who stays in his Arwing for air support in Assault
Star Fox 64: Arwing barrel roll deflects enemy fire; the Arwing has a force field and shields
Star Fox: Assault: Falco on the team; the team reaches the Aparoid homeworld; Fox destroys the Aparoid Queen

feats.claim: Flew Arwing air support for the Star Fox team through the Aparoid invasion and the assault on the Aparoid homeworld

campaignTags.claim: Ace Arwing pilot and Fox's wingman

unknowns: His solo combat record is not documented by the opened sources: the Aparoid Queen and Andross were defeated by Fox.

Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): replaced the generic Star Fox cite with opened pages on Falco, Star Fox 64 and Star Fox: Assault. Corrected the feat: Falco provided air support while Fox destroyed the Aparoid Queen, and the 'defeated Andross's forces' wording was dropped. Removed Smart Bombs and the hand blaster (Smash-only on the opened pages) and the unsourced on-foot weakness. powered-flight removed: his flight comes from piloting a vehicle, which the pilot tag already covers.

characters.continuity: Star Fox series (Star Fox 64, Star Fox: Assault)

In Star Fox: Assault he fights on foot with a blaster and picked-up weapons and destroys the Aparoid Queen.

techniques: Blaster and picked-up weapons on foot (Assault)

mechanisms: Arwing force-field shields and barrel-roll deflection

weaknesses: Not established by the opened sources
limitations: The Landmaster's barrel roll cannot reflect fire because it lacks the Arwing's force field

Fox shoots a program into the Aparoid Queen, pursues and defeats her; on-foot run-and-gun with a blaster and picked-up weapons; Arwing and Landmaster

feats.claim: Confronted and defeated Andross alone on Venom, killing his true brain form on the hard route
Pursued and defeated the Aparoid Queen, ending the Aparoid invasion

notableResults.note: Fought alone on Venom; easy route robotic Andross, hard route his brain form
Fox shot a self-destruct program into her and defeated her

campaignTags.claim: Pilots the Arwing and drives the Landmaster tank and Blue-Marine submarine

Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): replaced the unopened Wikipedia cite with opened Star Fox 64 and Star Fox: Assault pages. Corrected the Andross note: there is no 'core chamber after an aerial dogfight' on the opened page. Added the Aparoid Queen win. Removed the Reflector shield (Smash-only). characters.continuity: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
characters.summary: Ganondorf claims the Triforce, keeps the Triforce of Power, and turns Hyrule into a wasteland of fear during the seven years Link sleeps. He has potent magic, can fly and generate waves of darkness. In the final battle he is wounded, uses the Triforce of Power to become the beast Ganon and knocks the Master Sword from Link's hands, but Zelda holds Ganon at bay, Link lands the final blow, and the Seven Sages seal him away.

techniques: Ganon form melee (knocked the Master Sword from Link's hands)

mechanisms: Transforms into Ganon after apparent defeat

weaknesses: The Master Sword (Link's final blow in Ocarina of Time)
Zelda's sacred power held Ganon at bay
limitations: The Ganon transformation depends on the Triforce of Power

sources.supports: OoT: claims the Triforce, keeps the Triforce of Power, usurps Hyrule's throne; seven years later Link awakens; potent magic, waves of darkness, flight; final battle: transforms into Ganon with the Triforce of Power, knocks away the Master Sword, Zelda holds him at bay, Link lands the final blow, the Seven Sages seal him

feats.claim: Usurped Hyrule's throne and turned the kingdom into a wasteland of fear for the seven years Link was sealed away
feats.citation: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

feats.claim: As Ganon, knocked the Master Sword out of Link's hands
feats.citation: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

notableResults.citation: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
notableResults.note: Zelda held Ganon at bay while Link landed the final blow with the Master Sword; the Seven Sages then sealed him away

campaignTags.claim: Has potent magical abilities and generates waves of darkness
Uses dark magic, e.g. freezing Zoras in red ice

unknowns: The opened source does not describe a Triforce of Power invulnerability barrier or near-absolute durability, so both were removed.

Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): replaced the unopened Wikipedia cite with the opened Codex Gamicus Ganondorf page. Removed 'dark energy spheres', 'giant sword strikes', 'curse projection', the invulnerability barrier and 'arrogance' (not on the opened page). The conditional now says the Ganon transformation depends on the Triforce of Power. Tags magic and spellcaster kept.

characters.continuity: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
characters.formDifferences: After his second Demon King form is beaten, Ganondorf swallows his Secret Stone and loses his sense of self, becoming a gloom-filled dragon that flies and carries Link into the sky in its jaws. Its weak points are four eye clusters and the Secret Stone on its head.
characters.summary: The Demon Dragon is the draconified form Ganondorf takes by swallowing his Secret Stone. It carries Link into the sky and fights him there with Gloom and homing magical orbs. Link, with the Light Dragon's help, dives onto it, destroys its eye clusters, and shatters the Secret Stone on its head with the Master Sword.

techniques: Gloom contact (each hit permanently removes a heart until healed by sunlight)
Magical orbs launched at a diving Link

mechanisms: Large health pool (6000 HP) with weak points (four eye clusters, 1200 HP each) that must be destroyed before the Secret Stone is exposed

weaknesses: Four eye clusters on its body and the Secret Stone on its head
The Master Sword deals 10x damage to its weak points

sources.supports: Created when Ganondorf swallows his Secret Stone; carries Link upward in its jaws; Gloom contact costs hearts; slow; weak points: four eye clusters and the Secret Stone; Master Sword 10x damage; destroyed when Link shatters the stone; 'No trace of the original form remains'
After his second form is defeated Ganondorf swallows his Secret Stone, loses his sense of self, becomes the Demon Dragon and carries Link into the sky
Demon Dragon launches magical orbs; Link dives onto its back, fights in a gloom pool there, destroys the glowing weak points, then attacks the Secret Stone; the Light Dragon catches him

notableResults.citation: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
notableResults.note: Link shattered the Secret Stone with the Master Sword; the dragon died in an explosion of light

campaignTags.claim: Big enough to carry Link in its jaws and for Link to land and fight on its back, around a pool of gloom
Flies as a dragon, carrying Link up into the sky
Launches magical orbs and is filled with Gloom

unknowns: No opened page gives a measured size. giant-sized rests on the documented scale (Link lands and fights on its back), which the owner accepted on 2026-11-13 as meeting the documented-size ruling.
Mind: Zelda Wiki says he loses his sense of self and the in-game description says 'No trace of the original form remains'.

Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): replaced the unopened Tears of the Kingdom Wikipedia cite with Zelda Dungeon, Zelda Wiki and Nintendo Life. Removed 'gloom fire breath', 'tail swipes', 'dive bomb', 'durable scales' and 'gloom aura barrier' (not on the opened pages). The Light Dragon is Link's helper, not this form's weakness, so it was replaced by the documented weak points. Added the loss to Link.

characters.continuity: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
characters.formDifferences: His humanoid Gerudo form, restored from the mummified body sealed under Hyrule Castle. He fights with Gloom weapons (sword, spear, club, Demon King's Bow), perfect dodges, and in the second phase four Phantom Ganons. It is distinct from the mindless Demon Dragon.
characters.summary: Demon King Ganondorf awakens when Rauru's arm and Secret Stone fall near his sealed, mummified body, then uses his Gloom to restore a healthy Gerudo form. He fights Link with Gloom weapons and projectiles and perfect dodges. In his second phase he summons four Phantom Ganons, absorbs their Gloom and knocks out the Sages with a Gloom wave. Beaten, he swallows his Secret Stone to become the Demon Dragon.

techniques: Gloom Sword, Gloom Spear, Gloom Club
Gloom projectiles and homing magic orbs that permanently remove hearts
Gloom wave that knocks out the Sages
Updraft slam that erupts Gloom from the floor

mechanisms: Perfect dodges, including against parries and Flurry Rush
Knocks away arrows (first phase); not stunned by arrows in the second
Absorbs the Phantom Ganons' Gloom at half health

weaknesses: The Master Sword can deflect his Gloom projectiles (other weapons are destroyed by Gloom)
limitations: Not established by the opened sources

sources.supports: Awakened by Rauru's arm and Secret Stone falling near his mummified body; restores a healthy form with Gloom; Gloom weapons and bow; perfect dodges; four Phantom Ganons; Gloom wave knocks out the Sages; Master Sword deflects Gloom projectiles; swallows his Secret Stone after his second form is defeated
Phase 1 sword, spin, charge, spear and claymore attacks; phase 2 updraft slam erupting Gloom, Gloom bullets, homing magic orbs that permanently remove hearts

notableResults.citation: The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
notableResults.note: Defeated in both humanoid phases, after which he became the Demon Dragon

conditional.dependsOn: Awakening when Rauru's arm and Secret Stone fell near his sealed body, then restoring himself with Gloom

campaignTags.claim: Fights with Gloom weapons, Gloom projectiles and magic orbs
Summons four Phantom Ganons and releases a Gloom wave that knocks out the Sages

unknowns: Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): replaced the unopened Tears of the Kingdom Wikipedia cite with Zelda Wiki and Nintendo Life. Removed 'pure light attacks' (not on the opened pages) and 'reality warping' from the spellcaster claim. Corrected 'gloom armor absorption' to absorbing the Phantom Ganons' Gloom. Added the documented weapons, Gloom wave and the loss to Link. The range of his Gloom corruption across Hyrule is not covered by the opened pages.

characters.continuity: Mass Effect trilogy (as squadmate; Mass Effect 2 for powers and Archangel)
characters.summary: Garrus is a turian ex-C-Sec officer and long-range soldier who uses sniper and assault rifles with the Concussive Shot and Overload tech powers. As 'Archangel' on Omega he killed so many criminals that the Blue Suns, Eclipse and Blood Pack united to kill him. He was badly wounded by a gunship before Shepard's squad finished off the gangs.

techniques: Overload (EMP that heavily damages shields and synthetics)

mechanisms: Not established by the opened sources (fights from long range as squad support)

weaknesses: Not established by the opened sources
limitations: Overload's stun works only on synthetic foes whose resistances are down

sources.supports: Powers Concussive Shot, Overload, Turian Rebel, Armor-Piercing Ammo; assault and sniper rifles; long/mid-range soldier; ex-C-Sec officer
Archangel killed many of Omega's criminals and was targeted by the Blue Suns, Eclipse and Blood Pack; wounded by the Blue Suns gunship in the final fight
Overload inflicts massive damage on shields and synthetic enemies through an electromagnetic pulse; rank 2 briefly stuns synthetics whose resistances are down

feats.claim: As Archangel, killed so many of Omega's criminals that the Blue Suns, Eclipse and Blood Pack joined to hunt him; survived until Shepard's squad helped him finish the gangs, though a gunship wounded him

campaignTags.claim: Uses the tech powers Overload and Concussive Shot

unknowns: Owner ruling (2026-11-13): an electromagnetic-pulse power like Overload does not earn an electric tag.

Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): replaced the generic Mass Effect Wikipedia cite with opened Fextralife and GameBanshee pages. Corrected the Archangel feat: he was rescued alongside Shepard's squad and wounded by a gunship, not holding off the gangs 'independently'. Removed proximity mines, kinetic barriers, thermal clips and the unsourced turian-biology weakness. electric-control removed: the source describes Overload as an EMP tech power, not control of electricity.
